title: Renting? 7 Upgrades That Transform a Flat and Come Off the Wall
description: You can make a rental feel like yours without losing your deposit. Seven reversible upgrades that leave no trace when you move.
excerpt: You don't own it, but you live in it. Here are seven renter-safe upgrades that transform a flat and come off cleanly when you leave.
content:
Renting means living in someone else's beige box with a clause that says do not paint, do not drill, do not change anything. But a flat can feel like yours without a single permanent change — and without risking your deposit.

**Seven reversible upgrades**

1. **Peel-and-stick everything.** Removable wallpaper on one wall, adhesive tiles behind the sink. They come off cleanly and hide ugly surfaces underneath.
2. **Layered lighting.** Landlord ceiling lights are harsh. Add two or three warm plug-in lamps and the whole room changes.
3. **Tension rods.** Curtains, room dividers, even shelving — no drilling required.
4. **Rugs over bad floors.** A large rug hides worn laminate and warms a cold room instantly.
5. **Command hooks and strips.** Hang art and mirrors with zero holes.
6. **Swap the soft stuff.** Cushions, throws, bedding carry more of a room's personality than furniture.
7. **Plants.** The cheapest way to make a space feel alive and cared for.

**See it before you spend**

Rental budgets are tight, so mistakes hurt. Upload a photo of your flat to [RoomFlip](https://roomflip.io), test wall colors, rugs, and layouts, and see the result before buying anything. You commit only to what actually works in your space.

If you film rental makeovers, [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) dubs your videos into 50+ languages so your ideas reach renters everywhere.

You may not own the walls, but the space is still yours to live in well. Reversible upgrades let you make it feel like home — and take it all with you when you go.
